summary: No hard violations that block the wave. One documented-standard deviation is procedural rather than functional: the three fix-round commits (b39240c8, 509b22d7, ab6683c0) close with 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5' plus a 'Claude-Session:' line instead of WORK-ORDER.md rule 2's exact 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>' trailer -- a byproduct of this session's own attribution policy, not something a fix round can retroactively correct without rewriting already-made commits. Two Fowler 'Duplicated Code' judgement calls: the optional-argument-after-a-flag parsing shape is written out three times in scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs instead of one shared helper, and packages/db/scripts/migrate.mjs's redo branch re-states the ordinary apply loop's per-migration read/checksum/guard-check/push body for a single iteration instead of building one list both paths share. One TDD test-quality judgement call: migrate-redo.test.mjs's AC1 cell asserts the redone checksum equals migrationChecksum(editedSql) and migrationChecksum('create table ...') -- recomputing the expected value with the exact function migrate.mjs calls internally, a tautology by tests.md's own definition -- though it sits alongside a genuine, independent behavioural assertion (the redone function's live return value actually changed from 1 to 2), so the cell is not vacuous overall, only its checksum half is. No mocking-of-repo-controlled-code, no side-channel verification beyond the documented db-test convention (ledger row snapshots are the package's own prestate-pin idiom, exempted per the work order), and no evidence of horizontal slicing in the commit history (every ticket's implementation and its tests land in the same commit, never a separate red-tests-only commit).

findings.tickets_note: procedural, spans the #849/#957/#969 fix-round commits; not tied to one ticket's acceptance criteria
findings.rule_cited: WORK-ORDER.md rule 2: "Every commit message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`."
findings.summary: The three fix-round commits (b39240c8, 509b22d7, ab6683c0) end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus an added `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_...` line, not the rule-2 `Claude Fable 5.1` trailer the lane's own binding rule specifies. The six original ticket commits (f01b4d34..a4db0de2) do carry the correct trailer.
findings.evidence: git show -s --format=%B b39240c8 / 509b22d7 / ab6683c0 each end `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` + `Claude-Session: ...`; compare git show -s --format=%B f01b4d34 (etc.), which ends `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
findings.required_fix: Informational only -- rewriting already-made, already-reviewed commits to fix a trailer is a bigger risk than the deviation itself (and conflicts with the repo's own "never amend a landed commit" git-safety norm). Worth a one-line note to whoever runs the fix-round tooling for future waves: the attribution trailer a session's own harness appends can silently drift from the wave's WORK-ORDER.md rule.

findings.summary: Possible Duplicated Code: the "an optional value token immediately follows this flag, unless the next token itself starts with `--`" parsing shape is written out three separate times in the same file for three different flags (`--print-closure`'s module argument, `--retire`'s path argument, and `--ruling`'s value), instead of one shared helper the three call sites use.
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not a blocker. A small `optionalArgAfterFlag(argv, flag)` helper (return the next token unless absent or itself a `--flag`) would remove the duplication and the risk of the two copies drifting (as they nearly did -- RETIRE_RULING already skips the `--`-prefix guard the other two apply). Fine to leave as-is for a wave-1 lane; worth doing opportunistically next time this file is touched.

findings.summary: Possible Duplicated Code: the `redo` branch's single-item body (read file, compute checksum, run `assertNoTransactionControl`/`assertNoCheckFunctionBodyOverride`, push onto `pending`) restates the ordinary loop's per-migration body verbatim for one iteration, instead of the two paths sharing one push step over a list that differs only in how it is built (`[byVersion.get(redo)]` vs. `migrations.filter(m => !applied.has(m.version))`).
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not a blocker -- the two branches are short and the redo path is deliberately isolated per the header comment's own reasoning ("redo touches ONLY the named version"). A caller could instead compute `const targets = redo !== null ? [{ file: byVersion.get(redo).file, version: redo }] : migrations.filter(m => !applied.has(m.version))` once, then run the single read/checksum/guard/push body over `targets` for both paths, removing the five-line duplicate.

findings.summary: Per /tdd tests.md's own tautology definition ("expected value restates the implementation, so the test passes by construction"), the AC1 cell's checksum assertions recompute the expected value with the exact `migrationChecksum` function `migrate.mjs` calls internally to produce it, rather than an independent literal. If `migrationChecksum` itself always returned a constant, both these assertions would still pass.
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not a blocker -- the same cell also asserts `(await witness.query("select clara.redo_ac1_fn() as v")).rows[0].v === 2`, a genuine, independent behavioural check (the edited body actually ran) that a broken `migrationChecksum` could not fake, so the cell as a whole is not vacuous. The checksum-equality half specifically is testing bookkeeping consistency (ledger checksum reflects on-disk content) rather than the redo behaviour itself; a hard-coded literal hash, or dropping the checksum assertions in favour of the function-return-value check alone, would remove the tautology without losing coverage.
